task.title: Dependency completion propagation
task.specification: Config deps maps unique nodes to prerequisite-node lists and is a finite acyclic graph; IDs in deps always exist. Initially all nodes pending. Events poll,ok{id},fail{id}. A matching running node changes to done or failed; all other completion events are ignored. After each event, mark pending nodes blocked if any prerequisite is failed or blocked, transitively; then start every pending node whose prerequisites are all done, simultaneously in lexical order. Roots therefore start after the first event, not before it. Output {started:[newly started IDs in lexical order],states:{every node:pending|running|done|failed|blocked}}. No hidden cycle or undefined-node requirement exists. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}; initial state is null. Only the current event is available; each named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"run"}. Inputs have at most eight single lowercase ASCII-letter identifiers, safe integer quantities and at most 48 events. Return exactly the documented output fields after every event; state representation is unrestricted JSON. All identifiers and numeric fields shown in event forms are present; quantities and all intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. Regimes vary event order and timing: ordinary uses moderate capacity, boundary tests equality/empty cases, adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events, and shift uses smaller capacities or larger costs/delays within the same semantics. Generator regimes: Boundary uses independent roots; shift uses six nodes versus four with randomly sampled acyclic dependencies. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Theatrical lighting cue tracking
matchedCard.relation: A value entered in a sequence persists through later positions that contain no replacement for it. A new entry can therefore alter later states. A cue-only change limits that propagation by restoring the prior downstream value at the next position.
assumptions: The sequence uses tracking rather than independent complete states.
Explicit changes can be distinguished from values inherited from earlier positions.
matchedCard.boundary: An absent change is not an explicit reset. Forward-tracking and cue-only editing have different scopes and cannot be assumed interchangeable.
matchedCard.source_fact: ETC documents values tracking forward through cues and a cue-only operation that prevents an inserted or merged change from altering subsequent cues.

shuffledCard.label: Wetland flood storage
shuffledCard.relation: Temporary storage and slow release can spread an incoming surge over time and reduce a downstream peak. In a simplified flow balance, retained quantity changes with inflow and outflow; delaying movement does not by itself remove the incoming quantity.
assumptions: Release or another accounted outflow can restore capacity between surges.
Any other gain or loss is included in the flow balance.
shuffledCard.boundary: Storage alone cannot absorb a sustained excess of inflow indefinitely. A reduced peak is not evidence that the total incoming quantity disappeared.
shuffledCard.source_fact: EPA describes wetlands trapping and slowly releasing water, slowing runoff, and storing peak flows. The finite-capacity balance is an explicitly stated abstraction of storage behavior.

sources.title: Incorporating Wetland Restoration and Protection in Planning Documents

initial.explanation: A completion affects only a matching running node. After each event, repeatedly block pending nodes whose prerequisites are failed or blocked, then start all currently eligible pending nodes simultaneously in lexical order. Counterexample: starting a node whose prerequisite merely completed in the same event would violate the running-state requirement.
initial.mapping: For each node, state is one of pending, running, done, failed, or blocked; dependencies map prerequisite IDs to nodes. The returned started list is the lexical set transitioned pending→running after propagation.
initial.assumptions: Event type ok marks a matching running node done; fail marks it failed; all other completion events are ignored. Poll only triggers propagation and scheduling. Config remains available on every call.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;let d=input.config.deps,k=Object.keys(d).sort(),s={};k.forEach(x=>s[x]='pending');for(let z=0;z<output.length;z++){let e=input.events[z];if(e&&((e.type==='ok')||(e.type==='fail'))&&s[e.id]==='running')s[e.id]=e.type==='ok'?'done':'failed';let ch=true;while(ch){ch=false;for(let x of k)if(s[x]==='pending'&&d[x].some(q=>s[q]==='failed'||s[q]==='blocked'))s[x]='blocked',ch=true}let a=[];for(let x of k)if(s[x]==='pending'&&d[x].every(q=>s[q]==='done'))s[x]='running',a.push(x);let o=output[z];if(!o||JSON.stringify(o.started)!==JSON.stringify(a))return false;let t={};k.forEach(x=>t[x]=s[x]);if(JSON.stringify(o.states)!==JSON.stringify(t))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let d=config.deps,k=Object.keys(d).sort(),s=state?state.s:Object.fromEntries(k.map(x=>[x,'pending']));if(event&&(event.type==='ok'||event.type==='fail')&&s[event.id]==='running')s[event.id]=event.type==='ok'?'done':'failed';let ch=true;while(ch){ch=false;for(let x of k)if(s[x]==='pending'&&d[x].some(q=>s[q]==='failed'||s[q]==='blocked')){s[x]='blocked';ch=true}}let a=[];for(let x of k)if(s[x]==='pending'&&d[x].every(q=>s[q]==='done')){s[x]='running';a.push(x)}let t={};for(let x of k)t[x]=s[x];return {state:{s:s},output:{started:a,states:t}}}

final.explanation: Maintain each node's lifecycle in opaque state. For each event, complete only a matching running node; then repeatedly propagate blocked status through pending nodes. Finally, simultaneously start every eligible pending node in lexical order and return the complete state map.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){const d=config.deps,k=Object.keys(d).sort();const s=state&&state.s?state.s:{};if(!state)for(const x of k)s[x]='pending';if(event&&(event.type==='ok'||event.type==='fail')&&s[event.id]==='running')s[event.id]=event.type==='ok'?'done':'failed';let changed=true;while(changed){changed=false;for(const x of k)if(s[x]==='pending'&&d[x].some(q=>s[q]==='failed'||s[q]==='blocked')){s[x]='blocked';changed=true}}const started=[];for(const x of k)if(s[x]==='pending'&&d[x].every(q=>s[q]==='done')){s[x]='running';started.push(x)}const states={};for(const x of k)states[x]=s[x];return{state:{s:s},output:{started:started,states:states}}}

initial.explanation: Track each node’s lifecycle in state. For each event, accept ok/fail only when the node is running, propagate blocked status transitively, then start all eligible pending nodes in lexical order. Roots start only after processing an event.
initial.mapping: Nodes map to pending, running, done, failed, or blocked. Event completion changes only the matching running node; prerequisites determine blocking and eligibility.
initial.assumptions: Config is a finite acyclic dependency map with valid IDs. Events contain valid types and IDs when applicable. JSON values are finite and within stated limits.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){var d=input.config.deps,k=Object.keys(d).sort(),s={};for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)s[k[i]]='pending';if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(var e=0;e<output.length;e++){var ev=input.events[e],o=output[e];if(!o||!Array.isArray(o.started)||!o.states)return false;for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var id=k[i],st=s[id];if(ev.type==='ok'&&ev.id===id&&st==='running')s[id]='done';if(ev.type==='fail'&&ev.id===id&&st==='running')s[id]='failed';}var ch=true;while(ch){ch=false;for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var id=k[i];if(s[id]==='pending'&&d[id].some(function(x){return s[x]==='failed'||s[x]==='blocked';})){s[id]='blocked';ch=true;}}}for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var id=k[i];if(s[id]==='pending'&&d[id].every(function(x){return s[x]==='done';}))s[id]='running';}var exp=[];for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)if((o.states[k[i]]||'')!==s[k[i]])return false;for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)if(s[k[i]]==='running'&&(e===0||true)){var prior=true;for(var q=0;q<e;q++){} }for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var want=s[k[i]]==='running';if(want&&(!e||true)){} }if(Object.keys(o.states).length!==k.length)return false;}return true;}
initial.program: function solve(x){var d=x.config.deps,k=Object.keys(d).sort(),st=x.state?x.state.s:null;if(!st){st={};for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)st[k[i]]='pending';}else{var z={};for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)z[k[i]]=st[k[i]];st=z;}var e=x.event;if((e.type==='ok'||e.type==='fail')&&st[e.id]==='running')st[e.id]=e.type==='ok'?'done':'failed';var again=true;while(again){again=false;for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var id=k[i];if(st[id]==='pending'){var bad=false;for(var j=0;j<d[id].length;j++){var q=st[d[id][j]];if(q==='failed'||q==='blocked'){bad=true;break;}}if(bad){st[id]='blocked';again=true;}}}}var a=[];for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var id=k[i];if(st[id]==='pending'){var ok=true;for(var j=0;j<d[id].length;j++)if(st[d[id][j]]!=='done'){ok=false;break;}if(ok){st[id]='running';a.push(id);}}}var states={};for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)states[k[i]]=st[k[i]];return {state:{s:st},output:{started:a,states:states}};}

final.explanation: Maintain each node's lifecycle in opaque state. On each event, complete only a matching running node; stale or conflicting events are ignored. Then repeatedly mark pending nodes blocked when any prerequisite is failed or blocked, and finally start every remaining pending node whose prerequisites are all done, iterating IDs in lexical order. Roots therefore start only after the first event.
final.program: function solve(x){var d=x.config.deps,k=Object.keys(d).sort(),st;if(x.state&&x.state.s){st={};for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)st[k[i]]=x.state.s[k[i]];}else{st={};for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)st[k[i]]='pending';}var e=x.event;if((e.type==='ok'||e.type==='fail')&&st[e.id]==='running')st[e.id]=e.type==='ok'?'done':'failed';var changed=true;while(changed){changed=false;for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var id=k[i];if(st[id]!=='pending')continue;var bad=false,ds=d[id];for(var j=0;j<ds.length;j++){var q=st[ds[j]];if(q==='failed'||q==='blocked'){bad=true;break;}}if(bad){st[id]='blocked';changed=true;}}}var started=[];for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++){var id=k[i];if(st[id]!=='pending')continue;var ready=true,ds=d[id];for(var j=0;j<ds.length;j++)if(st[ds[j]]!=='done'){ready=false;break;}if(ready){st[id]='running';started.push(id);}}var states={};for(var i=0;i<k.length;i++)states[k[i]]=st[k[i]];return{state:{s:st},output:{started:started,states:states}};}

initial.explanation: Each event first completes only a matching running node, then repeatedly propagates blocked status, and finally starts all currently eligible pending nodes in lexical order.
initial.mapping: Graph nodes map to status values; prerequisite edges determine blocked propagation and eligibility. Running nodes alone can accept completion events.
initial.assumptions: The supplied graph is finite, acyclic, and references only declared nodes. Event fields are valid as specified; lexical order is ordinary identifier order.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var d=input.config.deps,n=Object.keys(d).sort(),s={};for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++)s[n[i]='pending';for(var k=0;k<input.events.length;k++){var e=input.events[k];if((e.type==='ok'||e.type==='fail')&&s[e.id]==='running')s[e.id]=e.type==='ok'?'done':'failed';var ch=true;while(ch){ch=false;for(var j=0;j<n.length;j++)if(s[n[j]]==='pending'){var q=d[n[j]],bad=false;for(var z=0;z<q.length;z++)if(s[q[z]]==='failed'||s[q[z]]==='blocked')bad=true;if(bad){s[n[j]]='blocked';ch=true}}}var a=[];for(var j=0;j<n.length;j++)if(s[n[j]]==='pending'){var q=d[n[j]],ok=true;for(var z=0;z<q.length;z++)if(s[q[z]]!=='done')ok=false;if(ok){s[n[j]]='running';a.push(n[j])}}var want={started:a,states:{}};for(var j=0;j<n.length;j++)want.states[n[j]]=s[n[j]];var got=output[k];if(!got||JSON.stringify(got)!==JSON.stringify(want))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var d=x.config.deps,n=Object.keys(d).sort(),s=x.state||{};if(!x.state)for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++)s[n[i]]='pending';var e=x.event;if((e.type==='ok'||e.type==='fail')&&s[e.id]==='running')s[e.id]=e.type==='ok'?'done':'failed';var more=true;while(more){more=false;for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++)if(s[n[i]]==='pending'){var q=d[n[i]],bad=false;for(var j=0;j<q.length;j++)if(s[q[j]]==='failed'||s[q[j]]==='blocked')bad=true;if(bad){s[n[i]]='blocked';more=true}}}var a=[];for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++)if(s[n[i]]==='pending'){var q=d[n[i]],ok=true;for(var j=0;j<q.length;j++)if(s[q[j]]!=='done')ok=false;if(ok){s[n[i]]='running';a.push(n[i])}}var v={};for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++)v[n[i]]=s[n[i]];return{state:s,output:{started:a,states:v}}}

final.explanation: Maintain each node's status in opaque state. For each event, complete a node only when it is currently running and the event is ok or fail. Repeatedly propagate blocked status through pending nodes, then start every remaining eligible node in lexical order. Return the complete status map and newly started list.
final.program: function solve(x){var d=x.config.deps,n=Object.keys(d).sort(),s=x.state;if(s===null){s={};for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++)s[n[i]]="pending"}var e=x.event;if((e.type==="ok"||e.type==="fail")&&s[e.id]==="running")s[e.id]=e.type==="ok"?"done":"failed";var again=true;while(again){again=false;for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++){var id=n[i];if(s[id]!=="pending")continue;var q=d[id],blocked=false;for(var j=0;j<q.length;j++)if(s[q[j]]==="failed"||s[q[j]]==="blocked"){blocked=true;break}if(blocked){s[id]="blocked";again=true}}}var started=[];for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++){var id=n[i];if(s[id]!=="pending")continue;var q=d[id],ready=true;for(var j=0;j<q.length;j++)if(s[q[j]]!=="done"){ready=false;break}if(ready){s[id]="running";started.push(id)}}var states={};for(var i=0;i<n.length;i++)states[n[i]]=s[n[i]];return{state:s,output:{started:started,states:states}}}
